purpose: Compare Axtroshastra's Compatibility (Milan / Ashtakoot Guna) report against AstroSage's Kundli Milan tool on the same birth data, to find where our model's koota scores, dosha calls, or verdict diverge from a well-established reference.

our_model.method: Classical Ashtakoot Guna Milan (8 kootas, max 36 points) + Moon-based Manglik (Mangal Dosha) check for each partner

reference_model.note: Enter both partners' name/DOB/TOB/place exactly as given in each test case's person1/person2. If AstroSage asks for gender explicitly, set Partner 1 = male/groom and Partner 2 = female/bride unless the test case's gender fields say otherwise.

results_summary_2026_08_06.raw_field_accuracy: 44/55 fields = 80.0% (8 kootas + total + 2 manglik flags, per case)

confirmed_bugs.detail: ('M','D') is 6, should be 5 (confirmed by TC01 + TC03, 2 independent matches). ('D','R') is 1, should be 0 (confirmed by TC04). The standard symmetric classical table (Deva-Manushya=5 and Deva-Rakshasa=0, either direction) matches AstroSage on all 3 data points.
confirmed_bugs.impact: Every koota-level mismatch in this sample (5 of 5 non-Manglik diffs) traces to this + the Vashya bug below — fixing both would bring koota/total accuracy to 45/45=100% on this sample.

confirmed_bugs.bug: Vashya table doesn't handle split signs
confirmed_bugs.detail: VASHYA is keyed only by whole moon-sign. Sagittarius and Capricorn are classical 'split' signs where the Vashya group depends on which half (0-15 deg vs 15-30 deg) the Moon falls in; our table always returns one fixed group per sign. Confirmed wrong on TC03 (Capricorn boy: AstroSage says Chatushpad/Q, we always return Jalachar/J for Capricorn).
confirmed_bugs.impact: Wrong ~half the time whenever either partner's Moon is in Sagittarius or Capricorn.

confirmed_bugs.bug: Manglik dosha is Moon-only; AstroSage/classical practice also checks Lagna (+ Venus)
confirmed_bugs.detail: 4 of 10 individual Manglik calls across TC01-TC05 disagreed with AstroSage (TC02 boy, TC03 boy, TC04 girl, TC05 girl) = 60% agreement. This is a KNOWN, already-documented limitation (see the report's own 'Moon-based check' caveat text in report_view.py:552-553) rather than a hidden bug, but the 40% disagreement rate is worse than expected and it flips the pass/fail marriage recommendation in TC03, TC04 and TC05.
confirmed_bugs.impact: Highest-value fix candidate: directly changes the headline verdict for real users, not just a sub-score.

results_summary_2026_08_06.recommendation: Fix the 2 GANA_SCORE entries and the Sagittarius/Capricorn Vashya split first (small, well-evidenced, mechanical fixes). Prioritize adding Lagna-based Manglik checking next — it's the one issue that changes the actual marriage recommendation, not just a koota point or two.
results_summary_2026_08_06.fixed_2026_08_06: GANA_SCORE and the Vashya split-sign handling were fixed in products.py (branch fix/milan-gana-vashya-accuracy) with regression tests in tests/test_milan_gana_vashya_accuracy.py using these exact TC01/TC03/TC04 pairs as fixtures. Re-running the comparison after the fix: 51/55 fields match (92.7%) — every remaining diff is a Manglik(Moon-only-vs-Lagna) case, which is a separate, larger, already-documented limitation, not yet fixed. Koota+total accuracy is now 45/45 (100%) on this 5-pair sample.

how_to_use: 1. For each test case below, enter person1 and person2 exactly as given into AstroSage's Kundli Milan form.
2. Record AstroSage's output into that case's `astrosage_result` block (leave nothing blank — use null only if AstroSage genuinely doesn't report that field).
3. Run the same two people through our own /en/compatibility funnel (or ask me to batch-run them through compute_milan directly) and fill `our_model_result`.
4. Leave `match` and `diff_notes` for the comparison pass — don't fill these by hand, they'll be computed once both result sets are in.
5. Send the completed JSON back; I'll diff every field and produce a summary of where/why the two models disagree.

result_field_shape.effective_guna: number 0-36 (after cancellation rules are applied, if the reference model reports this separately)
result_field_shape.verdict: string, e.g. 'Excellent match' / 'Very good match' / 'Acceptable match' / 'Not recommended'

test_cases.notes: Plain everyday case, both same city, standard daytime births. Sanity baseline before stressing edge cases. NAMES: Vaibhav (boy) / Riya (girl). Real Riya TOB entered on AstroSage was 04:40 (AM), not the 16:40 (PM) originally specified here — results below use the corrected 04:40 input on both sides for a fair comparison.
test_cases.diff_notes: Gana: we score Manushya(boy)-Deva(girl) as 6, AstroSage scores it 5 — confirmed bug in products.py GANA_SCORE[('M','D')], see TC03 for a second confirmation of the same bug. Everything else (including both Manglik calls) matches. Note: our 'effective_guna' (post-cancellation) isn't something AstroSage's free report surfaces, so that field can't be cross-checked here.

test_cases.notes: One partner born on 29 Feb (leap day) — checks date-handling around a calendar edge case that's easy to mis-parse. NAMES: Anshu (boy, Pune) / Nandini (girl, Mumbai, leap day).
test_cases.diff_notes: Every koota score matches exactly (leap-day date parsing is correct). Manglik(boy) disagrees: we say True, AstroSage says False. This is the Moon-only-vs-Lagna-based Manglik gap (see TC03/TC04/TC05 — 4 of 10 Manglik calls across this whole sample disagreed with AstroSage), not a date-parsing issue.

test_cases.notes: Birth time 23:55 — tests whether tz-to-UTC conversion accidentally rolls the date over (a classic off-by-one-day bug). NAMES: Golu (boy, Kolkata) / Pooja (girl). Real Pooja place entered on AstroSage was Mumbai, not Lucknow as originally specified here — results below use Mumbai on both sides for a fair comparison.

astrosage_result.verdict: Ashtakoot successful, but Mangal Dosha mismatch — consult an astrologer

test_cases.diff_notes: TWO confirmed bugs stack in this case: (1) Vashya: AstroSage's boy (Moon in Capricorn) reads as 'Chatushpad'(Q); our fixed per-sign VASHYA table always maps Capricorn->'J' (water), ignoring that Capricorn is a classical SPLIT sign (Vashya depends on which half of the sign the Moon falls in) — products.py:17. (2) Gana: same Manushya(boy)-Deva(girl)=6-vs-5 bug as TC01, second independent confirmation. (3) Manglik(boy): we say False, AstroSage says True — the Moon-only-vs-Lagna gap again, and this one actually flips the marriage recommendation.

test_cases.notes: Time of birth unknown for BOTH partners. Our engine defaults missing tob to 12:00 noon — confirm AstroSage does the same (or flags it), and that the resulting koota scores stay sane. NAMES: Rishi (boy, Jaipur) / Dimple (girl, Ahmedabad). CONFIRMED: AstroSage also defaults unknown TOB to 12:00:00 noon — same convention as ours.
test_cases.diff_notes: Gana: AstroSage's Deva(boy)-Rakshasa(girl) scores 0; we score 1 — confirmed bug in products.py GANA_SCORE[('D','R')] (currently 1, should be 0 to match the standard symmetric classical table). Manglik(girl): we say False, AstroSage says True — Moon-only-vs-Lagna gap again. Noon-default convention for missing TOB is confirmed identical between the two platforms.

test_cases.notes: Only one partner has an unknown birth time — mixed-precision pairing. NAMES: Akash (boy, Chennai) / Akansha (girl, Bengaluru, tob unknown -> noon).
test_cases.diff_notes: All 8 koota scores AND the total match exactly (14.5/36 both sides) — clean pass on the Ashtakoot math itself. Only Manglik(girl) disagrees: we say False, AstroSage says True — Moon-only-vs-Lagna gap again, and this one flips the marriage recommendation (AstroSage: NOT preferable; ours: Acceptable).

test_cases.notes: Birthplace in the US (DST-observing, tz -5/-4). Stresses non-IST timezone lookup and DST offset correctness — a common source of silent chart errors.
Birth date is a US DST spring-forward transition day (2004-04-04). If tz lookup uses a static offset instead of historical tz rules, this is where it breaks.
Gulf birthplace, fixed UTC+4 offset, no DST — simpler tz case as a contrast to TC06/TC07.
Southern-hemisphere birthplace with its own DST calendar (opposite season to the north). Also pairs cross-hemisphere with an Indian-born partner.
UK birthplace — tests the London tz/DST table (BST rules) plus a non-Indian-diaspora western-Europe case.

Degenerate case — both partners share the exact same DOB/TOB/place. Should read as same Nadi (likely Nadi dosha) and identical Moon sign/nakshatra. A good sanity check for whether same-chart comparisons behave sensibly on both platforms.

Same place & date, birth times only 12 minutes apart. Moon moves ~0.55° in 12 minutes — close enough that if either birth sits near a nakshatra-pada cusp, this can flip Tara/Gana/Nadi. Good precision stress test.

Same two real people as TC01 but entered in reversed order (bride first). Varna & Gana are direction-sensitive in our engine (see tests/test_milan_direction.py) — confirm the koota scores and total match TC01 exactly once gender is honoured, on both platforms.

Gender omitted entirely for both — our engine falls back to 'p1 = groom' by classical default. Confirm AstroSage's default assumption matches (it may require gender and force a choice, which is itself a finding worth noting).
1960s birth dates — tests ephemeris accuracy further back in time, and a generational pairing (e.g. for parents'-generation compatibility use cases).
Recent (2005/2006) birth dates — the newest end of the plausible user range for a marriage-compatibility product.
Smaller, less common Indian towns instead of major metros — stresses our gazetteer/geocoding lookup accuracy for lat/lon/tz (per QA_CHECKLIST.md §4, small towns are a known trouble spot).

No way to hand-guarantee a Manglik placement without running the ephemeris first, but these times/places were picked to maximize spread across Mars-sensitive Moon signs — flag if either/both come back Manglik on either platform and compare the cancellation reasoning given.
One partner overseas with a precise time, the other in India with no known time — combines two entropy axes (tz handling + missing-tob default) in one pairing.

US fall-back DST transition day (2003-10-26) plus a same-day year-end case for the other partner — second DST edge (fall-back can produce an ambiguous repeated local hour) to contrast with TC07's spring-forward case.
